policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'all that are round about him to help him' renders a noun of help with a third masculine singular reference, which both readings supply: qere עֶזְרוֹ and ketiv עזרה differ only in the mater for that suffix (ו vs. archaic ה), and the ketiv is vocalized to the same sense. No italicized supply and no ASV note is mapped to this unit, so the English distinguishes nothing; the qere base fallback carries the projection.
